title: WHO: ambient and household air pollution are associated with 6.7 million premature deaths a year
summary: WHO's air-quality fact sheet, dated 24 October 2024, gives that combined figure and a 2019 ambient figure of 4.2 million.
body: WHO's ambient air-pollution fact sheet, dated 24 October 2024, says that in 2019, 99 percent of the world's population was living in places where WHO air-quality guideline levels were not met. It says the combined effects of ambient and household air pollution are associated with 6.7 million premature deaths annually. It says ambient outdoor air pollution is estimated to have caused 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide in 2019, and that some 89 percent of those premature deaths occurred in low- and middle-income countries. The 6.7 million is the combined association the sheet states. The 4.2 million is the 2019 ambient estimate.
